question: Does long model-driven stimulus (each run's own prechecked reference model compared with the DUT every cycle) add verification sensitivity beyond the model-authored VERIFY tests?
population: the 23 analyzed delivered RF1b designs and the same deterministic single-point mutants as the RF1b mutation check (170 mutants before exclusions)

stimulus.reset: asserted on cycle 0, then with probability 0.01 per cycle
stimulus.inputs: each non-clock input keeps its value or takes a new uniform value: change probability 0.3 for 1-bit, 0.5 for wider

false_alarm_classification: both repeats of one case; output unresolved on cycle 0 because the specification leaves startup history open and the reset input unused; the model itself documents its first output as not guaranteed. Spec-open behavior, not an RTL defect: as a required gate it would push repairs against hidden-correct RTL.
notes: Mutants of the two false-alarm designs are excluded from the kill counts, as are invalid mutant runs.
All 5 VERIFY-only kills come from one timing-heavy design that the biased random stimulus did not drive deep enough.

The 9 mutants that survive every gate all look equivalent on inspection: comparison bounds the counters never reach, unused state-encoding relabels, an unreachable case default and a lint-only sink. This is inspection, not a formal proof; it means the VERIFY tests killed every apparently non-equivalent mutant in this population.
decision: RF2 not built: both predeclared criteria fail (2 false alarms > 1; 0 random-only kills < 2).
